codes.justification: Clause addresses holdback amount handling and placement in a joint account under lien legislation, part of payment mechanics.

The clause requires PITs to coordinate and optimize design elements (materials, building systems, constructability) in accordance with the Base Program through the Target Value Design process, addressing design consistency and coordination.

The clause establishes collaborative activities among PITs and PMT during design development, evaluating functionality, constructability and cost prior to construction, reflecting early team participation in Project development.

This clause establishes the Owner's right to engage Other Contractors or perform work with own forces in connection with the Project, affecting how the overall Work is organized and executed alongside the Contractor's performance.

The clause allocates contractual risk by reserving to the Owner the right to introduce other contractors or self-performed work, which affects coordination responsibility and risk allocation among parties on the Project.

The clause establishes the Contractor's responsibility for construction means, methods, techniques, procedures, and coordination of the Work, a broad execution obligation under the Contract Documents.
The clause expressly assigns responsibility for construction 'sequences' and coordinating the various parts of the Work, addressing sequencing of Work activities.
The clause explicitly references non-payment of compensation for Services as an example of the Owner's default, tying the termination right to payment obligations.
The clause allocates responsibility to the Owner for compliance and establishes a remedy mechanism (notice of default) when the Owner fails to meet its contractual obligations.
The clause directly addresses whether the Owner may withhold fees due to the Construction Manager, which is a payment mechanics issue.
The clause references variance from the Construction Cost Estimate, a cost-estimation/target mechanism, and clarifies it does not affect fee payment obligations.
The clause identifies grounds for termination based on the Owner's failure to pay certified amounts or provide financing evidence, directly implicating payment provisions.
The clause allocates risk to the Owner for defaults in contractual obligations, giving the Contractor a remedy of notice and potential termination.

The clause preserves the Trade Contractor's obligations for quality, correction, and warranty of work performed prior to termination, directly relating to correction of defective or non-conforming work.
The clause allocates continuing responsibility for conformity and correction obligations even after contract termination, an allocation of contractual risk.
The clause allocates responsibility for default and provides the SMT with a remedy of termination of a member's participation, managing risk of non-performance under the Contract.
This clause establishes the Construction Manager's overarching duty to control, direct, and supervise the Work to ensure conformity with the Contract Documents, a core work execution obligation.

The clause requires the Construction Manager, in consultation with Trade Contractors, to establish a date for finishing the Project after Ready-for-Takeover, addressing scheduling and sequencing of remaining work.
The clause imposes procedural duties on the Construction Manager to notify Trade Contractors and coordinate completion of the Project following takeover confirmation.

This clause governs the procedure following expiration of an arbitration agreement period, allowing referral of unresolved disputes to courts or other dispute resolution mechanisms including arbitration, directly addressing dispute resolution procedure.
The clause governs adjustment of the Contractor's Fee resulting from changes in the Work, directly tying compensation adjustments to the change mechanism.

The clause allocates risk of Owner insolvency by granting the Contractor a termination right, managing the risk of non-performance by the Owner.

The clause explicitly directs that the Contract Price and Contract Time be adjusted per GC 6.1, 6.2, and 6.3 (Change provisions) to compensate the Contractor for making good damage not its responsibility.

Clause addresses progressive release of holdback amounts, certification by the Payment Certifier, and timing of payment (30 calendar days), which are core payment mechanics.

Clause is part of Part 8 Dispute Resolution and addresses retention of rights and recourses tied to Notice in Writing requirements under the dispute resolution process, preserving parties' positions pending resolution.

The clause establishes a process for curing default and managing the risk/consequences of termination, allocating responsibility for correction within a defined process.
